title: Circuit breaker for rollouts using golden-prompt alarms
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective:
Build an automated circuit-breaker service that monitors quality regressions during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts by evaluating live traffic against a curated golden prompt set and scorecard. When a statistically significant regression is detected, the service must immediately trigger automated protections (stop ramp, route to fallback model, and create a high-priority incident).

Background and motivation:
We already run eval scorecards during scheduled tests and have a gated canary flow. However, a gap exists when regressions are only visible under real traffic distributions (e.g., long-tail prompts, tokenization edge-cases) or when a subtle quality drop accumulates during a slow ramp. This ticket implements a streaming, low-latency monitor that compares production responses against golden prompts and key metrics (semantic similarity, hallucination signals, API-level schema conformance) and integrates a conservative circuit-breaker into the rollout orchestration.

High-level design:
- Input stream: sampled copies of live requests and model outputs from canary/AB/shadow traffic (prefix-sampling + golden-prompt injection).
- Eval engine: run the same scoring functions used by offline evals (embedding-based similarity, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, hallucination classifiers, schema-validator).
- Statistical alarm: use sequential testing (CUSUM + rolling-window t-test) to detect sustained downward shifts in the golden-set mean score while controlling for false positives (target alpha ~0.01 per hour per canary).
- Circuit actions: on alarm -> immediate stop of further ramping, rollback to previous model variant OR route traffic to a defined fallback model or degraded compute tier; emit incident and create an auto-generated runbook link.
- Integration points: rollout-orchestrator (API hook to pause/resume ramps), Console (show live golden-set trend + last alarm), Alerts (PagerDuty + Slack), Audit log entry for compliance.

Instrumentation & metrics to track:
- golden_eval_mean, golden_eval_median, golden_eval_std (per-minute)
- alarm_state (OK | WARNING | TRIPPED), time_to_detect (seconds), false_positive_rate (rolling)
- rollback_count, manual_overrides_count, samples_evaluated

Configurable parameters (per-rollout):
- sampling_rate (default 5%)
- golden_set (named set id used for this rollout)
- detection_alpha and sensitivity (defaults tuned to reduce noisy rollbacks)
- min_samples_before_alarm (default 200 responses)
- fallback_model_id or fallback_policy (route | degrade)

Data retention and PII considerations:
- Keep only request metadata and model outputs for eval and tracing; redact user PII fields using the platform redaction pipeline before storage. Golden prompt set is curated to avoid PII. All audit logs and stored evaluations obey the customer data retention configuration.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Circuit-breaker service deploys in staging and receives sampled canary traffic.
2) Service computes golden-set scores in <3s per batch and stores per-minute aggregates into metrics pipeline.
3) Sequential test correctly detects a synthetic regression injected in staging within configured min_samples and triggers the pause action on the orchestrator API.
4) Console shows the golden-set trend, recent alarms, and a link to the incident / runbook.
5) Operator can acknowledge and override alarm from Console; override is audited.
6) End-to-end test added to the rollout integration tests verifying rollback and fallback routing.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (3 days): instrumentation & sampling: wire prefix-sampled traffic + golden-prompt injection in staging; simple scorer wrapper using existing eval libs.
- Phase 2 (5 days): implement sequential alarm logic (CUSUM + guardrails), expose a REST webhook to the rollout-orchestrator.
- Phase 3 (4 days): console UI surface + alerts + auditing + overrides.
- Phase 4 (2 days): hardening, add synthetic regression tests, production rollout behind feature-flag.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Too-sensitive alarms will reduce deployment velocity; therefore we bias towards lower sensitivity and require min_samples.
- Sampling bias: golden prompt injection vs natural distribution. We'll maintain both: dedicated golden-set injection and sampling of natural traffic to ensure coverage.
- Performance: scoring must be low-latency; heavy scoring will run in a separate evaluation worker pool to avoid adding tail latency to inference.

Open design decisions:
- Default fallback policy: rollback to previous pinned model vs do gradual degredation to cheaper quantized model. (Needs PM + SRE input).
- Whether to expose per-customer thresholds (multi-tenant complexity).

Related artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ROLL/Golden+Prompts+Circuit+Breaker (draft)
- Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/324
- Prototype notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-proto-link
- Rollout-orchestrator API spec: internal-api://rollouts/operations#pause

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on alarm sensitivity defaults, data retention language, and the console UX for overrides.
